title: Potato Dauphinoise
subtitle: French potato gratin baked in cream and garlic
excerpt: Thinly sliced potatoes layered in a buttered gratin dish, covered with garlic-infused cream, and baked until the top is golden and the potatoes are soft and have absorbed the cream into something silky and rich. One of the great side dishes of French cooking.

recipe.sourceNotes: Gratin dauphinois (dauphinoise in the Anglicised form) takes its name from the Dauphiné region of southeastern France. The traditional dish uses only potatoes, cream, garlic, and salt, with no cheese on top; versions with Gruyère on top are more common in restaurant cooking and are technically a gratin savoyard rather than a dauphinois. The potatoes must be sliced very thinly (2 to 3 mm) so they cook through before the cream reduces too much and scorches. A mandoline produces the most even slices. The cream can be infused with garlic, thyme, or bay before pouring over the potatoes.

content.text: Slice the potatoes as thinly as possible and do not rinse them; the surface starch helps bind the layers. The cream must be well seasoned and the garlic infused before pouring over. Cover the dish with foil for the first hour; removing it for the last 15 minutes allows the top to colour. The gratin should be made ahead and reheated; it improves overnight.

items.preparation: Maris Piper or Desiree; peeled and sliced 2 to 3 mm thin

content.text: Heat the oven to 160°C / fan 140°C / gas 3. Warm the cream, milk, garlic, thyme, nutmeg, salt, and pepper in a saucepan over low heat until steaming. Do not boil. Taste and adjust the seasoning; it should be well seasoned.

Butter a gratin dish generously. Layer the potato slices in overlapping rows, seasoning lightly between layers. Pour the warm cream mixture over the potatoes until they are just covered. Press down lightly. Cover with foil.

Bake for 1 hour. Remove the foil, scatter with Gruyère if using, and bake for a further 15 to 20 minutes until the top is golden and the potatoes are completely tender when pierced with a knife. Rest for 10 minutes before serving.
